vBRIEFInfo.author: overdeck/0.0.0
vBRIEFInfo.description: Plan for PAN-2420: pipeline merge fails with GitHub App 403 'Resource not accessible by integration' — merge door falls back to nothing

plan.title: Pipeline merge robustness against GitHub App 403 permission failures
plan.author: agent:claude-opus-4-8

narratives.Problem: The pipeline merge door authenticates as the overdeck-agent GitHub App. When the App installation lacks pull_requests:write / contents:write, the final merge PUT returns 403 'Resource not accessible by integration' (mergePullRequestWithAppPromise, github-app.ts:583). Three durable defects remain: (1) nothing verifies at boot that the App can merge — getMergeBackendStatus (github-app.ts:147) only checks credential-file existence, and generateInstallationTokenPromise (github-app.ts:206) discards GitHub's permissions object; (2) the merge door does not distinguish a permission 403 from a transient failure — forge.ts retry (227-300) and merge-ops triggerMerge step 4b transient check (merge-ops.ts:1167-1171) both miss it, so it lands as a generic merge_status='failed' with raw 403 text; (3) after an out-of-band merge following the 403, merge_status stays 'failed' and the pipeline respawns work+review+test agents against the merged branch. Root cause of (3) is a deadlock: reconcileStaleMergeStatus (deacon-merge.ts:145) processes merge_status='failed' and would detect the merged PR, but defers whenever a work/planning agent is active (deacon-merge.ts:226-235, PAN-1994 guard); the respawned work agent keeps hasActiveAgent true, and no dispatch site checks GitHub PR state before spawning. PAN-2402 sat as a zombie for 90 minutes.
narratives.Proposal: Three additive slices, no behavior removed. A) Boot preflight: surface the token permissions (FR-1), add verifyAppCanMerge() (FR-2), add warnIfAppCannotMerge() boot service mirroring merge-backend-health.ts's warnIfAutonomousMergeBackendUnavailable (called at main.ts:93) that names the missing scope (FR-3). B) Merge-door classification: add isIntegrationPermissionError() (FR-4) and, in merge-ops step 4b, record permission failures as merge_status='failed' with actionable mergeNotes naming the exact missing scopes from verifyAppCanMerge (FR-5) — the existing activity-entry emit on merge_status change (review-status.ts:485-494) is the needs-you surface. C) Reconcile + respawn guard: add shared shouldSkipDispatchAsMerged() wrapping verifyMergedBeforeLifecycle (FR-6), call it at advancing-role respawn sites so a merged branch is never re-dispatched (FR-7), and narrow the reconciler's PAN-1994 defer so a confirmed-merged PR terminalizes even when a non-planning (zombie) agent is active (FR-8). C's two beads close the deadlock from both ends, as the operator directed.
narratives.NonGoals:
- Not changing the GitHub App's actual installed permissions (operator already granted them 2026-07-06).
- Not adding a new merge_status enum value for permission failures — actionable mergeNotes on 'failed' is the surface.
- Not making bootReconciliationSkipReason (boot-reconciliation-predicates.ts:15) do a network PR-state check — it stays sync; FR-8 catches a briefly-resumed post-boot work agent within one patrol.
- Not guarding the swarm work-slot dispatch (deacon-swarm.ts:825) or merge-train conflict resolver (merge-train-deps.ts:70) — they dispatch against pre-merge branches during active work; file a follow-up if needed.
- Not weakening the PAN-328 in-flight-guard idempotency test or the PAN-1994 re-plan anti-contamination intent.

autoDecisions.summary: Needs-you surface = actionable mergeNotes on the existing 'failed' merge_status, not a new enum value.
autoDecisions.rationale: A merge_status change already emits an operator-facing activity entry carrying mergeNotes as details (review-status.ts:485-494). A new enum value would ripple through every merge_status consumer (derive gates, dashboard) for no added operator signal.

autoDecisions.summary: Dispatch guard reuses verifyMergedBeforeLifecycle via a thin named wrapper called at each respawn site, rather than centralizing inside spawnRun.
autoDecisions.rationale: spawnRun returns a run object every caller dereferences; making it return null or throw on a merged-PR skip is a wider, riskier contract change than a per-site early-return that each caller's existing continue/return control flow already supports.

autoDecisions.summary: Boot preflight warns, does not gate boot.
autoDecisions.rationale: The App scope is operator-fixable out-of-band; a hard boot failure would strand the entire dashboard over a merge-only capability. Matches the fire-and-forget warnIfAutonomousMergeBackendUnavailable pattern.

It is a synchronous predicate; adding a GitHub network read would change its contract. The steady-state reconciler (FR-8) terminalizes a merged branch within one patrol after boot, covering a briefly-resumed work agent.

items.title: Surface installation-token permissions from GitHub

expected_outputs: a test asserting InstallationToken.permissions is populated from the mocked create-token response passes

narrative.Action: Add a `permissions?: Record<string, string>` field to the `InstallationToken` interface (github-app.ts:32-35). In `generateInstallationTokenPromise` (github-app.ts:206-238), widen the response cast at line 233 from `{ token: string; expires_at: string }` to also include `permissions?: Record<string, string>`, and return `permissions: data.permissions` on the resolved token (alongside token/expiresAt). Do not change any caller; this is a purely additive field GitHub already returns on POST /app/installations/:id/access_tokens.

items.title: Given GitHub's create-installation-token response includes a permissions object, generateInstallationTokenPromise returns it on InstallationToken.permissions
Existing callers that ignore InstallationToken.permissions still compile — typecheck passes and their behavior is unchanged
Add verifyAppCanMerge() capability probe

expected_outputs: tests covering can-merge, missing pull_requests, missing contents, and not-configured cases pass

narrative.Action: Add an exported `verifyAppCanMerge(deps?)` that: returns `{ configured: false }`-style neutral result when `isGitHubAppConfigured()` is false; otherwise mints a token via the existing minting path and inspects `token.permissions`. Compute `missing: string[]` containing 'pull_requests:write' and/or 'contents:write' for any of `permissions.pull_requests !== 'write'` or `permissions.contents !== 'write'`. Return `{ canMerge: missing.length === 0, missing, detail }` with a human-readable detail string. Accept an injectable deps object (mirroring getMergeBackendStatus's MergeBackendStatusDeps pattern at github-app.ts:147) so the token mint and isConfigured are stubbable in tests. Do NOT hardcode a fallback; surface the real permissions.

items.title: When permissions include pull_requests:write and contents:write, verifyAppCanMerge returns canMerge:true and missing:[]
When pull_requests is missing/read, verifyAppCanMerge returns canMerge:false and missing includes 'pull_requests:write'; same for contents
When the GitHub App is not configured, verifyAppCanMerge returns a neutral not-configured result and mints no token
Boot preflight warns when the App cannot merge, naming the missing scope

expected_outputs: tests asserting warn fires with the missing scope named, and stays silent when canMerge or not-configured, pass

narrative.Action: Create `src/dashboard/server/services/merge-app-scopes-health.ts` mirroring the existing `merge-backend-health.ts` shape: an exported pure predicate `shouldWarnAppCannotMerge(result)` and an async `warnIfAppCannotMerge(deps = {})` that calls `verifyAppCanMerge()`, returns early when not-configured or canMerge, and otherwise calls `console.warn` (multi-line `[overdeck] WARNING: ...` via `.join('\n')`) AND `emitActivityEntrySync({ source: 'dashboard', level: 'warn', message: ... })` naming the missing scope(s) and the remedy (grant scopes on the installation). Wrap the body in try/catch like merge-backend-health.ts. Wire a fire-and-forget `void warnIfAppCannotMerge();` into main.ts immediately after the existing `void warnIfAutonomousMergeBackendUnavailable();` at main.ts:93. Inject warn/emit/getResult via deps for testing. This is not a boot gate — it only warns.

items.title: When verifyAppCanMerge reports missing:['contents:write'], warnIfAppCannotMerge emits a warn-level log and activity entry whose text names 'contents:write'
When the App can merge, or is not configured, warnIfAppCannotMerge emits nothing

main.ts invokes warnIfAppCannotMerge() as a fire-and-forget (void) call at boot, adjacent to warnIfAutonomousMergeBackendUnavailable, and the dashboard still logs its listen line without awaiting or gating boot
Add isIntegrationPermissionError() classifier

expected_outputs: tests asserting true for a 403 'Resource not accessible by integration' message and false for 409/timeout/ECONNRESET pass

narrative.Action: Add an exported `isIntegrationPermissionError(message: string): boolean` in github-app.ts that returns true when the message denotes a 403 whose body contains 'Resource not accessible by integration' (the exact string thrown by mergePullRequestWithAppPromise at github-app.ts:583, e.g. `GitHub merge failed: 403 {"message":"Resource not accessible by integration"}`). Match on both the 403 status token and the phrase to avoid false positives. Return false for transient signatures (ECONNRESET/ETIMEDOUT/timeouts) and for mergeable-state errors (405/409/422).

items.title: isIntegrationPermissionError returns true for a message containing '403' and 'Resource not accessible by integration'
isIntegrationPermissionError returns false for ECONNRESET, ETIMEDOUT, 'Timed out waiting for GitHub PR', and for 409/422 mergeable-state messages
Merge door records permission failures with actionable mergeNotes naming the scope

expected_outputs: a test asserting a permission-class merge error yields merge_status='failed' with mergeNotes naming the missing scope passes

narrative.Action: In merge-ops.ts triggerMerge step 4b's `if (!artifactMerged)` block (merge-ops.ts:1164-1187), before the existing `isTransient` branch, add a permission branch: `if (isIntegrationPermissionError(prMergeErr.message)) { const cap = await verifyAppCanMerge(); const scopes = cap.missing.length ? cap.missing.join(', ') : 'pull_requests:write, contents:write'; const note = \`GitHub App cannot merge — installation is missing ${scopes}. Grant these scopes to the overdeck-agent installation, then re-merge.\`; setReviewStatus(issueId, { mergeStatus: 'failed', readyForMerge: false, mergeNotes: note }); completePendingOperation(issueId, note); return { success: false, statusCode: 403, error: note }; }`. Import isIntegrationPermissionError and verifyAppCanMerge from ../../../../lib/github-app.js. Leave the transient and generic-else branches unchanged (superset, not replacement).

items.title: Given the artifact merge throws a 403 'Resource not accessible by integration', triggerMerge sets merge_status='failed' with mergeNotes that names the missing scope(s) and the remedy
The permission branch returns statusCode 403 and a distinct error string, not the raw '<forge> merge failed: ...' transient message
A transient (ECONNRESET) error still falls back to the existing verifying branch and a generic error still records merge_status='failed' via the unchanged else branch
Shared GitHub-authoritative pre-dispatch merged-PR guard

expected_outputs: tests asserting skip:true when the PR is merged and skip:false when open/absent/unresolvable pass

narrative.Action: In merge-verification.ts, add an exported `shouldSkipDispatchAsMerged(issueId: string, deps?): Promise<{ skip: boolean; reason: string }>`. It resolves the project internally via resolveProjectFromIssueSync(issueId); if unresolved returns `{ skip: false, reason: 'project unresolved' }`. It computes `branch = feature/<issueId-lower>` and calls the existing `verifyMergedBeforeLifecycle(issueId, projectPath, branch)`; returns `{ skip: result.merged, reason: result.reason }`. Any thrown error resolves to `{ skip: false, reason: '<error>' }` — a GitHub hiccup must never block a legitimate dispatch (fail-open). Inject the verify + resolve functions via deps for testing. This is the single read door for the merged-PR dispatch guard; downstream sites must call it rather than re-implementing PR-state reads.

items.title: When verifyMergedBeforeLifecycle reports merged:true, shouldSkipDispatchAsMerged returns skip:true with the merge reason
When the PR is open/absent (merged:false), shouldSkipDispatchAsMerged returns skip:false
When the project is unresolved or the GitHub read throws, shouldSkipDispatchAsMerged fails open with skip:false and a reason string
Skip advancing-role respawn when the PR is already merged on GitHub

expected_outputs: tests asserting each guarded site skips spawnRun when shouldSkipDispatchAsMerged returns skip:true pass

narrative.Action: Call `shouldSkipDispatchAsMerged(issueId)` and skip dispatch (with a logged + emitted reason) at the advancing-role respawn sites, immediately before the spawnRun call: (1) service.ts onIssueStateChangePromise (service.ts:283-310) — after the existing mergeStatus==='merged' terminal guard at :305, add the GitHub-authoritative check so a merged PR with merge_status!=='merged' is also treated as terminal; (2) deacon-review-status.ts orphaned test re-dispatch (before spawnRun at :587); (3) test-agent-queue.ts dispatchTestAgentAndNotifyPromise (before spawnRun at :85); (4) review-agent.ts spawnReviewRoleForIssuePromise (before spawnRun at :377). Each site uses its existing control flow to bail (return / continue / set an informative action). Do NOT touch swarm-slot (deacon-swarm.ts:825) or merge-train conflict resolver (merge-train-deps.ts:70) — see NonGoals.

items.title: service.ts onIssueStateChange skips the advancing-role spawnRun and logs a reason when shouldSkipDispatchAsMerged returns skip:true, even though merge_status is not 'merged'
The orphaned-test re-dispatch (deacon-review-status.ts) and test-agent-queue dispatch skip spawnRun for a merged PR and each records an informative action/note
The review-role dispatch (review-agent.ts) skips spawnRun for a merged PR, while an open/absent PR still spawns the review run normally
Reconciler terminalizes a confirmed-merged PR past a zombie agent

expected_outputs: tests asserting terminalize-past-work-agent and still-defer-for-planning pass

narrative.Action: Narrow the PAN-1994 defer in reconcileStaleMergeStatus (deacon-merge.ts:219-256). Today `hasActiveAgent` (deacon-merge.ts:226-235) is true when EITHER planning-<issue> OR agent-<issue> (work) is running, and any true value defers reconciliation. Change the defer condition so a confirmed-merged PR still terminalizes when the only active agent is a work/advancing (zombie) agent — defer ONLY for a genuine re-plan: an active planning-<issue> agent, OR a spec whose status is back at 'draft'/'proposed' (re-planning in progress; reuse the findSpecByIssue read already imported at deacon-merge.ts:162). When not deferring, keep the existing terminalize path (setReviewStatusSync merge_status='merged' + postMergeLifecycle at :237-255), which kills the zombie work-agent tmux session. Preserve PAN-1994's intent: do not contaminate a fresh re-plan. Keep the in-flight-guard idempotency intact.

items.title: Given a PR confirmed merged on GitHub with merge_status='failed' and only a running work agent (agent-<issue>), the reconciler sets merge_status='merged' and invokes postMergeLifecycle instead of deferring
Given a merged PR but an active planning-<issue> agent (or spec status draft/proposed), the reconciler still defers and does not overwrite merge_status (PAN-1994 preserved)
The reconciler still skips issues whose spec is completed/cancelled and preserves the existing PAN-1190 terminal guard unchanged
End-to-end: 403 door failure then out-of-band merge terminalizes with no respawn

expected_outputs: the integration test passes, asserting terminal merge_status='merged' and zero advancing-role spawnRun calls after the out-of-band merge

narrative.Action: Add an integration-style unit test that stitches the fixed paths with mocked GitHub reads: (1) the merge door hits a 403 permission error and records merge_status='failed' with a scope-naming note; (2) the PR is then reported merged on GitHub (out-of-band); (3) with the dispatch guard active, no advancing-role spawnRun fires; (4) reconcileStaleMergeStatus terminalizes to merge_status='merged' and calls postMergeLifecycle even though a work agent was 'running'. Mock verifyMergedBeforeLifecycle / PR-state reads and getAgentStateSync; assert final merge_status and that the spawnRun spy was not called for review/test after the merge. Use fake timers if any delay/retry path is exercised (NFR-3).

items.title: Given a 403 permission failure at the merge door, the door records merge_status='failed' with mergeNotes naming the missing scope
After the out-of-band merge, no advancing-role spawnRun is invoked and reconcileStaleMergeStatus records merge_status='merged' and calls postMergeLifecycle despite a running work agent
